subject.title: [Feature]: Lightweight subagent instruction files (à la Claude Code .claude/agents/)

question: Should OpenClaw core add label-backed subagent role-profile files for `sessions_spawn`, and if so what security and precedence contract should they have?
rationale: This cannot be resolved as a narrow bug fix because it adds a trusted prompt/config surface that can change tool capability, model/provider selection, memory behavior, and audit provenance for child sessions.

options.title: Design core role profiles
options.body: Add the feature only after maintainers define the core lookup, precedence, narrowing-only tool policy, model/provider limits, memory, and audit contract.

options.title: Route to plugin/ClawHub
options.body: Keep core unchanged and document how a plugin or bundle can implement role-file prompt append with existing hooks, accepting that built-in `label` lookup remains absent.

options.title: Reject the new surface
options.body: Close the direction and keep `agents.list`, explicit `agentId`, attachments, and inline tasks as the supported ways to express subagent identity.

recommendation.title: Design core role profiles
recommendation.body: Add the feature only after maintainers define the core lookup, precedence, narrowing-only tool policy, model/provider limits, memory, and audit contract.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history on the central subagent/session runtime and docs surfaces and appears best positioned to decide the core-versus-plugin boundary.
